thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated SRV lookup failures and intermittent service discovery divergence in us-west1 / failover to us-west1b. SRV failure rate ~40% observed since 04:11 UTC. Paging eng-oncall.

emma (eng-oncall): taking this. reading graphs now. any customer hits yet?

incident-bot: Observed signals: 
- SRV lookup SERVFAIL and occasional stale SRV answers from some resolvers.
- Consul/etcd agent reconnects on subset of control-plane hosts.
- Automated health checks show mixed success between us-west1a and us-west1b.
Sample logs:
``` 
04:10:58 coreDNS[svc]: lookup svc-cache._tcp.svc.cluster.local -> SERVFAIL
04:11:03 consul: agent: rpc: heartbeat timeout waiting for server
04:11:07 kube-proxy: failing healthcheck to api-server us-west1a (timeout)
```

rahul (netops): seeing a routing flap between us-west1a and the regional fabric at ~04:08-04:12. AS-paths briefly changed; some routes moved to alternate POP causing asymmetric return paths. Provider notes show partial control-plane partition affecting tcp/session affinity on our NATs.

tia (sre): are we seeing split DNS caches? coreDNS in us-west1a appears to be serving outdated SRV records for a handful of services, while us-west1b answers are fresh. Could be due to inconsistent consul snapshots pushed to local caches during the flap.

pablo (platform): deploy-bot shows a small canary push to coredns config at 04:05 adjusting 'max_concurrent' to 200. Not sure if related. Rolling back the canary now: `deploy-bot rollback coredns/us-west1a --to=previous`

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated for coredns/us-west1a.

emma (eng-oncall): jen, any customer tickets?

jen-support: Support queue: 6 customers reported increased API latency and 2 reported failed job scheduling. Marking high-touch for the two enterprise accounts. Posting initial status: "Investigating service discovery issues in us-west region; mitigation in progress."

tia (sre): immediate mitigations I'll run: 1) force CoreDNS cache flush in us-west1a, 2) rotate coreDNS pods to clear stale upstream state, 3) check consul snapshot propagation and force an authoritative sync if necessary. Running: `kubectl -n kube-system exec -it coredns-0 -- kill -HUP 1` and `kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/coredns --context=us-west1a`

rahul (netops): pushing temporary route policy to prefer stable peering via POP-B for control-plane traffic to avoid the asymmetric path. Also increasing BGP hold timers briefly to avoid rapid churn: `bgp neighbor * timers 30 90` (applied to edge routers). Provider engaged and investigating the fabric flap root cause.

consul-bot: consul: leader election detected old=consul-2 new=consul-3 at 04:11:24, raft-commit-latency=720ms

pablo (platform): I'm pinning the Consul leader to consul-3 for the duration to prevent repeated elections until the network stabilizes; applying override via ansible group vars. Also increasing `rpc_timeout` to 2s to absorb transient network jitter.

tia (sre): after cache flush and pod rotation, SRV failure rate dropped from 40% -> 12% in 4 minutes. Some stale answers remain for ~2 services. Running a script to compare SRV responses across AZs: `./scripts/diff-srv-responses --services=critical --regions=us-west1a,us-west1b`

emma (eng-oncall): good. rahul, any timeline on provider confirmation?

rahul (netops): provider confirmed they saw a spine switch over and partial route withdrawal 04:07-04:13 due to a maintenance fiber reseat. They claim they restored uniform ECMP at 04:14 and are still running diagnostics. I opened a high-priority ticket for detailed routing dumps.

jen-support: posting update to customers: "Mitigations applied; brief window of service discovery inconsistencies in us-west region from ~04:08-04:15 UTC. Some internal API calls retried; two enterprise customers were affected and have been contacted by support. No data loss."

consul-bot: consul: agent reconnects down to baseline. raft stable.

pablo (platform): verifying KV consistency now; running `consul operator raft list-peers` and `consul snapshot validate`. KV checksums match across datacenter replicas.

tia (sre): final SRV error rate at 04:18 is 0.6%. I'll leave probes running for 60m. We'll need postmortem items: - why coredns canary coincided with network maintenance, - cache invalidation propagation under partial partition, - Consul leader pin rationale and config changes.

emma (eng-oncall): setting severity Sev2 -> Monitoring at 04:20 UTC. Assigning owners: emma=timeline + detection, rahul=network root cause & provider coord, tia=consul/dns remediation & artifacts, pablo=platform config diffs & rollback plan, jen=support comms.

rahul (netops): follow-up: schedule 1:1 with provider for 13:00 UTC to review their maintenance process and our scheduling/visibility. Will ask for RIB dumps.

pablo (platform): follow-up: revert transient config overrides after 24h observation and add a gating rule for coredns canaries to check network path stability metric before rollout. Filing PLAT-6240.

jen-support: closing impacted support tickets after verification; will follow up with the two enterprise customers.

tia (sre): uploading logs and artifacts to s3://redwood-incidents/2945678901/ including `srv-diff` output, consul raft logs, coreDNS pods logs and the canary diff.

emma (eng-oncall): Creating postmortem: https://redwood.internal/pg/postmortems/new tag network/dns/route-flap. Drafting summary and next steps.

incident-bot: Incident status changed to Monitoring at 04:20 UTC.

emma (eng-oncall): handing off on-call in 35m; will keep synthetic probes running 1h. If anything regresses reopen thread. Great coordination team. :thumbsup:
